newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hapoalim bidder said Israel investment worthwhile.
newsitem.headline: Hapoalim bidder said Israel investment worthwhile.

text.p: A group led by U.S. banker Jeffrey Keil that is bidding for Israel's Bank Hapoalim said in a statement on Sunday it believed it was worthwhile investing in Israel.
"My partners and I believe it is worth investing in Israel and we will do so in a very substantial manner," said Keil.
The Keil-Fishman group is one of the two seeking a controlling stake in Israel's Bank Hapoalim. Last week the group made a deposit of 40 million dollars required to bid for a stake in the bank.

The group comprises Israeli entrepreneur Eliezer Fishman, Alliance Tire Co, Darban Investments Ltd, T.L.C. Finance and Management, Leucadia National Corporation, Eurofrance S.A, and the banker Edoard Stern. Lazard Frers is the adviser to the group.

The Israeli government controls 78 percent of Hapoalim with the remainder traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. It aims to sell between 25 percent and 69.3 percent through the tender which it hopes to complete by mid-August.
